ingredientGroups.heading: The beef and the first stage

ingredients.item: lean beef , one piece, tied if it wants to fall apart
ingredients.preparation: eye of round, brisket point's lean half, or shank

ingredients.item: garlic , crushed, and a thumb of ginger , sliced — the poaching aromatics
bird's eye chilies , whole, stems on

instructions.heading: The poach (40 minutes)
instructions.action: The poach (40 minutes). The beef in cold water with the aromatics, brought to the barest simmer — a bubble every few seconds, 90 °C-plus but never a rolling boil (a hard boil tightens the fibers this recipe is trying to shred) — skimmed once at the come-up, lid ajar, 40 minutes to just-tender.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: a chopstick slides into the meat with firm resistance — cooked through, not yet falling. Lift the beef to a board (save the liquid — it is stage two's base), rest it 10 minutes, and slice across the grain into 5 mm strips, then tear the strips by hand into shreds along the fibers. The hand-tearing (not knife-cutting) is what gives jangjorim its signature fibrous pull.

instructions.heading: The braise (25–30 minutes)
instructions.action: The braise (25–30 minutes). The shredded beef, soy, 150 ml of the poaching liquid, syrup, mirin, the ten garlic cloves, and the chilies into the wide pan — at a steady simmer now, lid off, stirring every 5 minutes as the liquid reduces.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: at 20 minutes the liquid has dropped below the beef's level and the pan's sounds deepen from bubbling to a slow sizzle; the shreds are turning glossy mahogany and the garlic has gone amber at its edges. The target is a wet-not-soupy mass — spoonable with liquid just filling the gaps, not a dry stir-fry and not a stew.

instructions.heading: The jar and the month
instructions.action: The jar and the month. Off the heat, sesame oil and seeds through, and pack into a clean glass jar while hot — the residual heat and the salt content are the keeping. Cool uncovered, then lid and refrigerate.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: the eating test, warm from the pan and again cold from the fridge on day three: the shreds should pull into long savory-sweet strands, the garlic crushes into them like a paste, the chili sits whole for the brave — and over hot rice, one spoonful should make the bowl disappear faster than anything else on the table. That is the rice-thief standard, and this jar meets it.

visualDonenessCues: The poach: barest simmer, 40 minutes, skimmed — never a rolling boil.
The shred: hand-torn along the fibers, 5 cm lengths, never knife-diced.
The braise: reduced to wet-not-soupy, shreds glossy mahogany, garlic amber and soft.
The jar: packed hot, cooled uncovered, clean dry spoon forever.
storageNotes: The jar keeps 3–4 weeks refrigerated. The braise is the make-ahead, portioned by the week. The spent braising liquid's next career: eggs (#B19's entire recipe).

Variations: the quail-egg batch (#B19); braised shiitake alongside the beef for the two-texture jar; a spoon of jangjorim over a plain fried egg is the single best rice bowl this site's whole banchan section produces.
